name: Economics (PhD)

rules.desc:
• Students must be enrolled in courses in accordance with departmental expectations stated in the Handbook. When students reach 135 units, they must have completed all degree requirements, except for the oral exam and dissertation submission, and must request Terminal Graduate Registration (TGR) status.

• Failure to meet degree requirements, including the department's grade expectations, may lead to dismissal from the program.
rules.name: Enrollment and TGR
Graduate Core
rules.desc: The graduate core consists of three different sequences taken in the first year of the program. Petitions to substitute courses must be approved by the DGS prior to the start of the quarter. Waiving out of any core course must be submitted via the online form for instructor approval at least two weeks before the start of the term.

rules.name: Fields of Specialization
rules.desc: Students should read all specifics about each year’s field requirements on the Economics department website for non-course-related requirements toward the field. Courses may not be double-counted towards requirements of multiple fields. Any substitutions must be pre-approved by the DGS.

children.name: Econometrics

MGTECON 614
MGTECON 661
MS&E 328
300+ level courses in Statistics or Computer Science, approved by faculty

children.name: History/Institutions
children.notes: Grades of B+ or higher is required.

children.name: Microeconomic Theory
children.desc: At least one course must be either 282 or 286.

rules.name: History Requirement
rules.desc: This requirement must be completed during the student's second year of study. If history is a student's field of specialization, they will replace this requirement with an additional breadth course (moved in by hand).

rules.name: Breadth Requirement
rules.desc: • Complete a minimum of one course in at least two fields other than the students' fields of specialization. Breadth courses cannot be cross-listed in a student’s fields. If History is one of your fields of specialization, the student is required to take one class in a third additional field outside of the student's specializations.

rules.name: Additional Coursework Requirement
rules.desc:
Students must complete eight courses in total during their second year. Depending on the combination of fields chosen, the student may need to take one additional course to meet the eight-course requirement. The additional course may be taken in any of the fields of specialization, including their own. Students may also choose from the approved Econ grad courses not found in the fields of specialization as listed on the website.

• With advance approval of the Director of Graduate Studies, some of these courses may be drawn from related fields taught in other departments. Permission needs to be obtained from the Director of Graduate Studies before enrolling in a course outside the department if the student wants it to count towards requirements.

rules.name: Second-Year Paper
rules.desc: All students must submit a second-year paper by August 31 of their second year in the program, and they must arrange for a faculty member to oversee the paper by the end of the spring quarter of the second year. A draft submission is due three weeks prior to this date.

rules.name: Seminar
rules.desc:
• Third-Year Seminar: presentation of an expanded research paper in the spring quarter of the third year.

• Seminar Participation: Each student is expected to enroll and participate in at least one all-year research seminar or three quarters of the same field seminar by the end of the fourth year of residence. Usually, participation in a seminar requires one or more oral presentations and the submission of a research paper (which, however, need not be completely separate from dissertation research). Detailed information on fulfilling the seminar requirements can be found on the Economics department website.

rules.name: GPA of 3.0, a B average in each core sequence, and B or better in PhD-level courses

rules.desc: Teaching is core to the academic and professional training of doctoral students in our program. All students are required to complete one quarter of teaching experience in the Economics department by the end of their fourth year in the program, regardless of their financial support. Typically, students complete more than the required number of teaching quarters as part of their professional training and financial support.
rules.name: Teaching Requirement

rules.desc: Admission to candidacy is a prospective judgment by the faculty of a student’s potential to successfully complete the requirements of the degree program. Students are expected to complete qualifying procedures and apply for candidacy by the end of August of their second year. Qualifying procedures in the Department of Economics include required coursework and the second-year paper. Additional details on qualifying procedures can be found in the Graduate Handbook on the department website.
rules.name: Advancement to Candidacy

rules.desc: In the Department of Economics, the oral exam is a defense of the dissertation presented upon the completion of a substantial portion of the dissertation or upon completion of a pre-final draft. Students consult with their dissertation advisor and reading committee members on the timing of the defense. Students are expected to complete this milestone by the end of their sixth year in the program.
rules.name: Oral Exam

rules.desc: Students are required to submit an approved dissertation that makes an original contribution to Economic scholarship. This may include three separate papers. Students are expected to submit the dissertation by the end of their sixth year in the program.
rules.name: Dissertation

gpa: All graduate students should have an average grade point average of 3.0, which is the equivalent of a B average.
grading:
• Students in the Department of Economics are expected to earn a minimum of a B in all PhD-level coursework unless otherwise stated.

• In the graduate core courses, taken in the first year of the program, students are expected to earn at least a B, as is the baseline for our program. However, we acknowledge that the first year can be an adjustment, so each individual course must be completed with a grade of B- or higher, and the average of the three courses in each field (microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics) must be at least a B. Grades of B- or below are considered inadequate. All such grades are reviewed by the Director of Graduate Studies (DGS) and may require the course to be retaken. Any grade of C+ or lower will always necessitate a retake. If a course must be retaken, the DGS will specify the grade required to be considered satisfactory progress.

• Except in rare cases, satisfactory progress requires no more than two of the following to appear on the transcript at any given time: Incomplete (‘I’), Not Passed or No Credit (‘NP’ or ‘NC’), grades of B- or below, or Withdrawn (‘W’).
transferPolicy: Students who completed graduate coursework at another institution are strongly encouraged to transfer course units in the winter quarter of their first year of doctoral study. The Registrar will evaluate the transfer of units on a course-by-course basis. Graduate work accepted for transfer of residency does not automatically exempt a student from having to complete a course requirement for the degree.
reviewNotes: Each core course in microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics needs a B- or better, and the History/Institutions field needs a B+ or better. Microeconomic Theory as a field must include ECON 282 or 286. Your advisor checks the 3.0 GPA, the B average in each core sequence and the B expected in other PhD-level courses, and you move in by hand the two breadth courses, the eighth second-year course, and the breadth course that replaces the History Requirement when History is one of your fields. The second-year paper, seminars, teaching, candidacy, oral exam and dissertation are milestones the department records.
